pages.en:
Perhaps the tension holding me together snapped when Tohsaka left.

My feverish body suddenly feels leaden, and I lie down where I am in the living room.

“——”

I stay on my side and wait for the returning nausea to pass.

「……マスター同士の戦い、か」
それが一体どういうものなのか、自分にはまだ判らない。
はっきりしているのはこの手に余る、という事だけだ。
少しでも聖杯に興味があるのなら、もう少し実感が湧くのだろうが

Tick by tick, the second hand marks time in the silent room.

“…A battle between Masters, huh.”

I still don't understand what that really means.

All I know for certain is that it is beyond me.

If I had even the slightest interest in the Holy Grail, perhaps it would feel more real—

pages.ja:
「何故だろう。聖杯には、嫌悪感しか湧かない」
望みを叶えるという杯。
それがどんなモノかは知らないが、サーヴァントなんていうモノを呼び出せる程の聖遺物だ。

“Why is it? All I feel toward the Holy Grail is disgust.”

A cup said to grant wishes.

I don't know what manner of thing it is, but it must be a sacred relic of tremendous power if it can summon beings like Servants.

俺はそんなモノに興味はない。
実感が湧かず半信半疑という事もあるのだが、結局のところ、そんな近道はなんか卑怯だと思うのだ。

Even if it cannot truly grant any wish whatsoever, it is valuable beyond measure to a mage.

And yet—I have no interest in such a thing.

Partly because it feels unreal, leaving me doubtful it even exists. But more than that, a shortcut like that simply feels like cheating.

「それに、選定方法が戦いだっていうのも質が悪い」
……だが、これは椅子取りゲームだ。
どのような思惑だろうと、参加したからには相手を押し退けないと生き残れない。
その、押し退ける方法によっては、無関係な人々にまで危害を加える事になる。

“And choosing its owner through a fight makes it even worse.”

…But this is a game of musical chairs.

Whatever your intentions, once you enter, you must force the others aside to survive.

And depending on how a participant chooses to do that, innocent people may be harmed as well.

pages.ja:
だから、
喜べ衛宮士郎。
俺の戦う理由は聖杯戦争に勝ち残る為じゃなくて、
君の望みは、ようやく叶う。
どんな手を使っても勝ち残ろうとするヤツを、なんとしてでも止める事。

Therefore—

—Rejoice, Shirou Emiya.

My reason to fight is not to survive the Holy Grail War.

—Your wish will at last be granted.

It is to stop, by any means necessary, those who would do anything to win.

“——”

Another wave of dizziness strikes.

Of course it does.

My body may look whole again, but only a few hours ago it was nearly cut in two.

There is no reason I should recover immediately. Frankly, it would be easier to believe I would remain like this for the rest of my life.

力のない者が戦いに参加すれば、傷つくのは当然だ。
俺は己の力量不足の代償として体を失いかけ、
彼女は、そんな俺を守るために傷を負った。

pages.en:
I nearly died three times in a single day.

Those without power cannot enter a battle and expect to go unhurt.

I nearly lost my body as the price of my own inadequacy.

And she was wounded protecting me from it.

“——!”

I bolt upright.

遠坂が居間に居座っていた事ですっかり失念していた。
いや、無意識に考えるのを避けていた。
卑怯者。
自分の為に傷ついた誰か、
無惨に血を流す少女の姿を、思い返す事を避けていた。

“That's right—she…!”

What am I doing?

I had completely forgotten because Tohsaka occupied the living room.

No. I had unconsciously avoided thinking about it.

—Coward.

I refused to remember the person wounded for my sake—the girl bleeding so terribly before my eyes.

「遠坂のヤツ、肝心なコトは外しやがって……！」
休んでいた体に喝を入れて立ち上がる。
遠坂はセイバーについて何も語らなかった。
俺をセイバーと二人で運んだ、なんて言いながら、それ以上の説明はしなかった。
一番に聞かなくてはいけない事、バーサーカーの手で負傷した彼女が、無事なのかと言う事を。

“Damn it, Tohsaka! You left out the one thing that mattered…!”

I force my resting body to its feet.

Tohsaka said nothing about Saber. She told me the two of them carried me home, then offered no further explanation.

There was one question I should have asked before any other: whether the girl Berserker wounded was safe.

Fighting the dizziness, I search the house.

No, before that—

“…They call me her Master, but what part of me is fit to be Saber's Master?”

I have no idea who Saber is, or by what principles a being like a Servant exists.

It's like handing a tank to a raw recruit.

“…Stop wallowing, you idiot. That was an unforgivably rude piece of self-pity.”

In my mind, I bow my head to the blond girl.

And suddenly I cannot rest until I find her and make certain she is safe.

“——Could it be?”

An idea occurs to me without warning.

Not the house, not the garden, and not the storehouse where we first met.

Come to think of it, there is one other large building on the estate.

急ぎ足で歩き出す。
向かう先は離れにある剣道場。

“That must be it. I'm sure she's there.”

I set out at a hurried pace.

My destination is the detached kendo dojo.

“——”

A thread of tension runs through me.

If she is not there, I will have no choice but to admit that she has disappeared.

“…?”

And then I notice it.

I know absolutely nothing about her—yet here I am, contradicting myself by wanting someone so unknown to remain.

“——”

The space is perfectly still.

The sunlight entering it is white and immaculate, joining her and the dojo into a single whole.

There is not the slightest break in her straight, dignified posture.

Her presence alone draws the air in the dojo taut.

Yet there is nothing cold about it.

There is such purity in the sight of her that I forget even the cold winter air.

“——, ——”

Even the sound of my catching breath is an intrusion.

And this is the result.

I became Saber's Master and was dragged into the slaughter called the Holy Grail War.

Not a single part of it reflected my own will.

I am only a half-trained mage swept into a battle far beyond his station—

Whatever the circumstances, I have chosen to fight.
